create.name: Bhante Buddharakkhita
create.bio:
Bhante Buddharakkhita is a Theravada Buddhist monk from Uganda, often described as the country's first native-born monk. He grew up in a Christian family in Kampala and came across the Buddha's teachings in 1990 while he was a student in India. In 2002 he took full ordination with the late Sayadaw U Silananda in San Jose, California, then spent eight years as a student of Bhante Henepola Gunaratana, living at his West Virginia monastery, the Bhavana Society. In 2005 he founded the Uganda Buddhist Centre near Entebbe, which he still leads as abbot and which has grown to include schools, a nunnery and village projects alongside its meditation programme.

He has taught mindfulness and insight meditation across Africa, North America, Asia, Europe and South America, and teaches Theravada Buddhism at Union Theological Seminary in New York. His dhamma talks are plain-spoken and often funny, drawing on his own unusual path to look at fear, happiness, emptiness and the freedom of a settled heart. He is the author of four short books, among them Planting Dhamma Seeds, an account of bringing the dhamma to Africa, and Sowing Seeds of Peace, a practical meditation guide for daily life; the centre makes all four free to read online.

courses.title: Thanksgiving Insight Hybrid Retreat
courses.description: The online, livestreamed version of the IMS Thanksgiving insight retreat, taught by Tuere Sala, Bhante Buddharakkhita and Shelly Graf. Home participants follow sitting and walking periods and dharma talks broadcast from the Barre meditation hall; beginners and experienced meditators are both welcome.

free_resources.title: Sowing Seeds of Peace: Mindfulness Meditation for Finding Peace Within
free_resources.description: Bhante's practical handbook on bringing mindfulness meditation into ordinary days, offered as a free PDF by the Uganda Buddhist Centre. It walks through basic sitting practice and the attitudes that support it.

free_resources.title: Planting Dhamma Seeds: The Emergence of Buddhism in Africa
free_resources.description: His memoir of meeting the Buddha's teachings in India and returning to Uganda to found a Buddhist centre, shared free as a PDF. It traces the early years of Theravada practice taking root in East Africa.

free_resources.title: Drop by Drop: The Buddha's Path to True Happiness
free_resources.description: A short introduction to living the dhamma day to day, built around the idea that steady small efforts gradually fill the vessel. Free to read as a PDF from the Uganda Buddhist Centre.

free_resources.title: Caring for Our Planet: Buddhism and the Environment
free_resources.description: A free-distribution booklet on what Buddhist ethics and interdependence ask of us in caring for the natural world. Available as a free PDF.
